title: After the service: Paul Barbarin and the Famous Door group
summary: Back in 1946 he played with Paul Barbarin for six months, then at the Famous Door with Edgar Blanchard, vibes and bass.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Uh, were there any other bands in there we could go back to your life after you played, uh, you say you played with Kid Howard there for a while? And then, uh, any other, the more or less Dixieland type bands, or dance bands you played with after that that you can remember?
Well, I worked around with, uh, around town with, uh, Manny Gabriel. Uh-huh. He's in, uh, yeah.
Yeah. Well, you played with Paul Barbera? Right after coming out of the service, I played with Paul Barbera. Yeah, I never heard you in those days, you see.
Yeah. I never, didn't live here. Uh-huh. Well, when did you get out of the service, about? 46th.
Then you were playing straight with Paul Barbera.
Right after I came out of the service.
Did you use mostly a chord style with him, that is the regular rhythm? Or did you play, uh, feature solos then too? How did you do that?
Well, he admired my single spring work, I think, and solo work.
Yeah. I used to do a lot of that with him. But, you know, change and mental all the time. I think I worked with him at six months, you know? At six months. You know, that's...
I worked at the famous door with Edgar Blanchett, and two guitars, and...
Remember the names of the other fellows that were in the group?
Well, we had Dawgert Dawson and Vibes. Stuart Davis, played bass with us. And Edgar was the other guitar player. Yeah. Edgar got his own band and... I was in my Natal, I think.
